body: Credibility-generated forward test (NOT a recommendation; not buy/sell). Probability 0.56 (naive sector base rate 0.57) that: Sansera FY27 consolidated revenue growth is >=17.0% (low end of 'high-teens' guide). Probability set only by the pre-stated rule (research_notes/Promise tracker pilot/AUTO_COMPONENTS_peer_comparison.md section 5): p0 = 0.57 (leave-one-out peer strict delivery rate, category 'revenue_growth', n=23); SAC -4.8 pts x weight 0.286 (N=8) -> p = 0.56. Evidence: Q1FY27 call (13-Aug-2026): 'we expect to end FY27 with high-teens top-line growth'; Q&A 'high-teens to 20%'; Feb-26 'about 20%'. Screener: FY26 3,498 cr; H1FY27 2,112 cr (+33%); needs H2 >= ~1,981 cr (+3.9% YoY). ADS FY27 guide INR 550-600 cr. Resolution: YES if FY27 consolidated revenue from operations / FY26 - 1 >= 17.0% (NSE XBRL + screener consolidated, one decimal). Source: NSE XBRL + screener.in consolidated. Resolve by 2027-05-31; score with Brier vs the base rate, to test whether the credibility adjustment adds skill.

data.adjustment_applied: p0 = 0.57 (leave-one-out peer strict delivery rate, category 'revenue_growth', n=23); SAC -4.8 pts x weight 0.286 (N=8) -> p = 0.56
data.adjustment_rule: p0 = leave-one-out pooled STRICT delivery rate (specificity-weighted share 'delivered'; partly=0) of the other 4 peers in the promise's category (all-category peer rate if <8 peer promises in that category). p = clip(p0 + N/(N+20) x SAC/100, 0.05, 0.95), N = company's scored promises, SAC in points (credit basis: delivered 1, partly 0.5; categories with n<5, or with <2 peers having data, pooled). P(base) = p0.
data.base_rate_reasoning: Naive forecaster = sector delivery rate for 'revenue_growth' promises among the other auto-component peers (strict: delivered only, specificity-weighted; n=23). No company-specific information.
data.resolution_rule: YES if FY27 consolidated revenue from operations / FY26 - 1 >= 17.0% (NSE XBRL + screener consolidated, one decimal).

title: Paper call: Sansera FY27 consolidated revenue growth is >=17.0% (low end of 'high-teens' guide)
